chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Haytham, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Breast-feed your child with the milk of the good (women), and beware of the bad (fornicatress), for the milk indeed transmits (qualities/traits).'

key_terms.الْحِسَانِ: The good/virtuous (feminine plural, referring to wet nurses)
key_terms.الْقِبَاحَ: The bad/ugly (feminine plural, referring to less virtuous or promiscuous women)
key_terms.يُعْدِي: Transmits/contagious (implies transmission of traits or qualities)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of choosing a virtuous wet nurse in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises selecting a virtuous wet nurse, emphasizing that milk transmits not just physical nourishment but also the nurse's inherent moral and spiritual qualities to the child. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view of 'al-hisan' (beauty/virtue) and 'al-qibah' (ugliness/flaws) as encompassing both physical appearance and inner character, highlighting the profound impact of early environmental influences on a child's development.
